families.sequence: Merman draws the participant types (actor, boundary, control, entity, database), box and fragments like the reference; current prints the @{type} metadata as participant text and hides the box label. Merman dark paints the box light grey (#d3d3d3), hiding the messages inside it.
families.class: Current is clean on the inheritance fixture but drops notes, the interface stereotype, and a member in the second. Merman's layout follows the reference but its labels are clipped at both ends (fixable, see methodology), and its dark theme loses compartment dividers.
families.state: Merman matches the reference's stacked composites and paired transitions, with clipped labels. Current offsets one composite, overlaps the Turn on/Turn off labels, and puts the initial dot over a note label.
families.er: Merman matches the reference layout and type-first attribute order, with clipped names; its dark rows alternate pure black. Current uses another layout and attribute order; in dark one relationship label sits under an entity.

Current fails one input Mermaid.js and Merman render (merge of a branch with no own commit).

methodology: Current column: biscuit_visualized::mermaid::MermaidDiagram::render (format SVG, scale 1) with MermaidTheme::Dark or ::Default, so it includes today's gitGraph merge repair, tag spacing, and SVG fixes (D26). BISCUIT_VISUALIZED_CACHE_DIR points at a fresh temp dir before every timed iteration, outside the timed region, so every render is a cache miss.

Current timings therefore include the cache's existence check, directory creation, the SVG write, and the spike's read-back of the file. That file-system work is measured alone with the same steps and shown as 'cache I/O'; the 'net of cache I/O' ratio subtracts it. On macOS it is most of the measured time (about 0.24 of 0.32 ms).

Merman column: merman @ 482fcde7faffb05a466f198085d615e604075d97, default-features off, features svg + all-diagrams + layout-cytoscape (no ELK), SvgPipeline::resvg_safe(), site config {"theme": "dark"} or {"theme": "default"} (Mermaid's built-in themes, no compiled theme or palette work). One Renderer per theme is built outside the timed region.

'Merman (real fonts)' column: Merman measures text through our TextMeasurer, installed with Merman's public TextMeasurementProfile API (merman::svg::{TextMeasurementProfile, TextMeasurementPolicy::uniform}, SvgEnvironment::with_text_measurement_policy), which shapes each label with usvg 0.45 using the rasterizer's font database. Measuring and drawing resolve faces with one function (src/fonts.rs FontChain::resolve): MERMAID_FONT if set and installed; the label's font-family stack in order, names matched ignoring case; the OS's generic answer from fontique (fontconfig, CoreText, DirectWrite), mapped to fontdb by file path and face index; else the first face (by family name, path, index) whose OS/2 sFamilyClass or PANOSE classifies it. No overflow fix is applied. Two corrections stay: the gradient-stroke fix (fix_merman_svg) and the sans-serif answer as usvg's default for text with no font set.

Merman's wrapping helper is not exported by the facade, and TextMeasurer::measure_wrapped's default ignores max_width, so our measurer wraps with a plain greedy word wrap. Merman's own native measurement (native-fonts feature: NativeFontOptions with the font files of the faces the chain resolved, SvgEnvironment::with_native_font_context) gives the same defect counts on both hosts; it is shown in the measurer comparison, not as a column.

Label clipping with Merman's default measurement: each label sits in a nested <svg style="overflow:hidden"> sized from Merman's built-in, font-free measurement, and the faces drawn are wider. Measuring with the drawn faces removes it (218 → 2 on macOS, 268 → 2 on Linux), with no change to the SVG's clipping.

Timing: warm (one untimed warm-up render), in-process, release build, single thread, 25 iterations per input on the dark theme; median and p95 of those. Rasterization is not included; it is measured once per PNG and shown separately as 'raster'. Family figures: median of per-input medians, and the largest per-input p95, over inputs both renderers drew.

Rasterization: both columns go through the same code (a copy of biscuit-visualized's resvg 0.45.1 path: default usvg options, system fonts loaded once, uniform scale to 2x the SVG's natural width, capped at 1000 px). The gallery embeds those PNGs after a lossless ImageMagick recompression (pixel-identical).

Panels: today's renders paint their own background (#020617 dark, white light). Merman's PNGs are transparent; in the dark gallery they sit on a fixed dark surface (#16181d), as they would on a dark terminal. Mermaid.js references always sit on white.

References: Merman fixtures carry Mermaid.js 12.2.0 references from Merman's fixtures/upstream-svgs. Our test diagrams and the four gitGraph cases use the local mmdc (Mermaid CLI 11.12.0, default theme). Inputs mmdc rejects (non-zero exit or its syntax-error diagram) are treated as invalid Mermaid and excluded from the family status counts; Merman rejects exactly the same nine inputs.

Cross-OS (R-S9): today's renderer measures text with the host's fonts, so its layout changes size between macOS and Linux for most inputs; Merman's layout uses its own text metrics and keeps the same pixel size on both hosts for all but two images, differing only in glyph rendering. Windows was not run. Linux figures were re-run after the generic-family fix; the first Linux pass had no Merman text and its cross-OS numbers were invalid.

Corpus: 43 Merman fixtures (23 shared families, 14 Merman-only), 4 gitGraph cases from docs/mermaid-gitgraph.md (R-S7), and 56 unique Mermaid sources extracted from the repo's Rust tests by scripts/extract_test_diagrams.py. Sources built by format! with interpolated values cannot be extracted statically and are not included.

Merman's own export: scripts/merman_cli_survey.py runs merman-cli (same rev) with --svg-pipeline resvg-safe on every Merman fixture and gitGraph case, both themes, and surveys its SVGs with the same detector. With Merman's default deterministic text measurement it reproduces the defects (208 clipped labels, 36 invisible zero-area lines), and its own PNGs show them; 62 of 94 of its SVGs are byte-identical to the library output the spike uses, the rest differ only in layout geometry.

Browser check: the resvg-safe SVGs for the class and ER fixtures, opened in headless Chrome, clip the same labels (class 15 of 15, ER 27 of 29; "Animal" is 51.3px of text in a 44.8px box, with Chrome resolving "trebuchet ms" to Trebuchet MS). In the dark theme Chrome also resolves the divider stroke to the objectBoundingBox gradient, so the dividers are missing there too. Both defects are in Merman's resvg-safe output, not specific to resvg.

Why Merman's playground looks clean: its default workspace (playground/src/lib/workspace-snapshot.ts) uses svgPipeline "parity" (HTML labels in foreignObject, mounted inline in the page, so a label is not boxed into a fixed-width clip), textMeasurementMode "browser", diagramFont "trebuchet", Mermaid config {} and diagramTheme "auto" (Mermaid's default, light theme unless dark is chosen). The gallery uses the resvg-safe pipeline, Merman's deterministic measurement, and Mermaid's stock dark and default themes in Merman's default neo look, so differences from the playground are pipeline and theme differences, not rendering bugs in themselves.

MERMAID_FONT: unset or empty, step 1 is skipped with no log. Set to an installed family (matched ignoring case), every label uses it. Set to a family that is not installed, one warning names it and resolution continues with the font stack. See the MERMAID_FONT demo.

Host dependence: with real fonts, layout follows the fonts installed on the host, not the OS. Between macOS and Linux the real-fonts SVG width changes by a median 0.5% (90th percentile 5.9%, largest 18.7%), and 122 of 188 PNG pairs change pixel size; Merman's default measurement changes almost nothing (2 of 188), and today's renderer changes about as much as real fonts. This is expected, not a defect: goldens for real-font output belong per host, or with a pinned font set.
remaining_defects: Swimlane edge label "Needs code change" (2 label renders per host): Merman's layout wraps it to two lines and sizes its box for two lines, but the resvg-safe conversion emits the label as one line of SVG text, so it is cut whatever font measures it. Merman's issue (resvg-safe foreignObject fallback drops line breaks of wrapped HTML labels).
Radar legend (6 past their shape, 2 outside the canvas) and one gitGraph tag on Linux: the detector pairs these labels with an unrelated shape; likely false positives, unchanged by measurement.
Stock dark-theme contrast (sequence box, pie, radar, packet, treeView, usecase note): theme, not measurement; the planned palette and contrast work (D6, D18) addresses it.
